audit_items.proof_trace: Data columns are saved to storage during block proposal (receive_data_column.go:10) BEFORE state transition validation occurs in ReceiveBlock. The RPC handler retrieves columns directly from storage (line 123) without checking if the parent block passed state transition. A proposer can create a block that fails state transition but has cryptographically valid data columns; these columns will be stored and served to peers despite the invalid block.
audit_items.attack_scenario: Attacker proposes a block with invalid state transition (e.g., incorrect epoch processing, invalid validator operations) but valid data columns. The block proposal flow (proposer.go:325-334) runs ReceiveBlock and ReceiveDataColumns in parallel. Even when ReceiveBlock fails state transition, data columns are already stored (receive_data_column.go:10). Peers requesting these columns via P2P DataColumnSidecarsByRoot will receive sidecars for an invalid block, wasting network bandwidth and potentially causing reconstruction failures.
